summary.short: OMB Memorandum M-26-04 requires US federal agencies to include contractual requirements addressing the Unbiased AI Principles in new LLM procurements, requires vendor transparency documentation, and mandates updated agency procurement policies by March 11, 2026. It excludes national security systems and sunsets two years after issuance.
summary.long: OMB Memorandum M-26-04, dated December 11, 2025, implements a directive in a July 2025 executive order on Preventing Woke AI in the Federal Government. The executive order sets two Unbiased AI Principles for large language models (LLMs): truth-seeking and ideological neutrality. The memorandum applies to each executive department, military department, independent establishment and wholly owned Government corporation, and not to national security systems. Agencies must include contractual requirements addressing compliance with the principles in any LLM solicitation or order issued after the memorandum's date, and should modify existing LLM contracts where practicable before any option extends performance. By March 11, 2026, agencies must update procurement policies, including processes for agency users to report outputs that violate the principles. Appendix A sets a minimum vendor disclosure set (acceptable use policy, model, system or data cards, end-user resources, and a feedback mechanism), a further set of enhanced disclosures an agency may request, and states that compliance may be designated material to contract eligibility and payment. The memorandum does not govern regulatory actions on non-agency AI uses, assessments of AI providers that are targets of enforcement, or incidental contractor AI use. It ceases to have effect two years after issuance unless the OMB Director provides otherwise.

thresholds.note: The memorandum sets no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Its scope is defined by reference to 5 U.S.C. 101, 102 and 104(1) and 31 U.S.C. 9101 without a number. The headings 'Minimum Threshold for LLM Transparency' and 'Threshold for Enhanced LLM Transparency' name content tiers, not numeric values. The March 11, 2026 deadline and the two-year sunset are procedural time limits coded as events, not thresholds.
